items.title: Neuropsychiatric Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus or Obesity.
items.authors: Jani HT, Levine H, Patel A, Trivedi R, Patel XD.

sections.text: Neuropsychiatric safety concerns about glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and tirzepatide prompted regulatory review by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). We synthesized the contemporary evidence in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus or obesity, emphasizing study design, risk of bias, and the distinction between signal detection and causal inference. The PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases were searched without a lower date limit through March 15, 2026 (English, adults ≥18 years). The review was reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, and the PRISMA-S and PRISMA-Harms extensions. Evidence was grouped into prespecified categories: randomized syntheses, comparative observational studies and target-trial emulations, outlier non-active-comparator studies, pharmacovigilance analyses, and regulatory reviews. Risk of bias was appraised with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and with Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Interventions; certainty was summarized using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Twenty studies and two regulatory reviews met the inclusion criteria. Randomized evidence, including two large 2025 meta-analyses and post hoc pooled analyses of semaglutide and tirzepatide, showed no increased risk of suicidality, depression, or anxiety, though psychiatric exclusion criteria limited generalizability. Active-comparator cohorts from the United States, Scandinavia, and the United Kingdom likewise showed no clear increase after confounding control. Passive-comparator and disproportionality analyses generated signals but could not separate drug effects from baseline psychiatric risk, obesity-related distress, or reporting bias. The EMA and FDA conclusions do not support a causal class-wide association between GLP-1 RAs and suicidal ideation or behavior. Evidence does not support a clinically meaningful increase in neuropsychiatric harm with GLP-1 RAs or tirzepatide in the populations studied. Surveillance remains warranted for patients with substantial psychiatric morbidity, for obesity-only populations, and for long-term rare outcomes.

items.title: Adaptation to university life, fear of loneliness, and depression in first-year students at a private university in the Peruvian Amazon: a structural equation model.
items.authors: Gebol-Checàn R, Ascorbe-Peña G, Miguel-Mariño R, Tapullima-Mori C, Cjuno J, Mayta-Llanos J.

sections.text: The transition to university is a period of heightened psychological vulnerability. This study aimed to examine the association between adaptation to university life, fear of loneliness, and depression in Peruvian first-year university students. A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted with 345 participants selected through non-probability convenience sampling at a single private university in the Peruvian Amazon. The Student Adaptation to College Questionnaire, the Brief Scale of Fear of Loneliness, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 were administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The proposed model showed an adequate fit [χ² (516) = 1,478, p < 0.001, CFI = 0.940, RMSEA = 0.074, SRMR = 0.069]. Personal-emotional adjustment (β = 0.49, p < 0.001) and social adjustment (β = 0.29, p = 0.003) were positively associated with fear of loneliness, whereas academic adjustment (β = -0.34, p < 0.001) and institutional adjustment (β = -0.22, p = 0.001) were negatively associated; in turn, fear of loneliness was positively related to depression (β = 0.81, p < 0.001). Significant gender differences were found in institutional adjustment [t (343) = 2.597, p = 0.010, d = 0.29] and personal-emotional adjustment [t (343) = 3.076, p = 0.002, d = 0.34], with women reporting higher levels than men. The findings position fear of loneliness as a key affective link between first-year students' adjustment to university and their depressive symptoms, suggesting that early detection and intervention programs focused on adjustment, implemented during the first year, could help mitigate depression in this population.

items.title: Distinct Associations of Age and CYP2D6 Genotype With Parent Venlafaxine Exposure and O-Demethylation in Japanese Psychiatric Patients.
items.authors: Ishihara Y, Sasaki T, Asahi T, Ono Y, Sugisaki T, Hiramatsu R, Kawamata Y, Sugawara N, Yasui-Furukori N.

sections.text: Venlafaxine (VEN) is converted to O-desmethylvenlafaxine (ODV) mainly through CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation. However, age-related clinical factors may also influence VEN exposure in routine practice. We examined whether age and CYP2D6 genotype show different associations with parent-drug exposure and metabolic conversion. This retrospective therapeutic drug monitoring analysis included 78 Japanese psychiatric patients with available plasma VEN and ODV concentrations and CYP2D6 genotype data. Two prespecified outcomes were analyzed without body-weight correction: VEN concentration divided by daily dose (VEN/dose) and the ODV/VEN ratio. CYP2D6*10 and *5 were coded as reduced- and no-function alleles, respectively. Log-transformed outcomes were analyzed using regression models including age and CYP2D6 reduced/no-function allele count. Nineteen patients (24.4%) were aged 65 years or older. Age was correlated with VEN/dose (Spearman rho = 0.295, p = 0.0086), and older patients had higher VEN/dose than younger patients (median, 0.522 vs. 0.192 [ng/mL]/[mg/day], p = 0.0127). In regression analysis, the incremental R2 for age was numerically larger than that for CYP2D6 allele count for VEN/dose (incremental R2, 0.058 vs. 0.026). Conversely, the ODV/VEN ratio was strongly associated with CYP2D6 allele count (standardized beta = -0.391, p < 0.001; incremental R2 = 0.145) but not with age. Age-by-genotype interactions were not significant for either outcome. Age appeared to be more closely related to dose-corrected parent VEN exposure, whereas CYP2D6 genotype predominantly determined the ODV/VEN metabolic ratio. The relative contribution of age should be interpreted descriptively because no formal comparison of effect sizes was performed. Separating exposure and metabolic-ratio outcomes may clarify how geriatric and pharmacogenetic factors contribute to VEN disposition.

items.title: Kinesiophobia following ACL reconstruction: a qualitative netnographic study of lived experiences shared on Reddit.
items.authors: Kahve Y, Darben Azarsiz Y, Aydin S, Aydin T, Gurhan U, Civan Kahve A.

sections.text: Kinesiophobia, broadly defined as fear of movement and vulnerability to (re)injury, is one of the most significant psychological barriers to functional recovery following anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, yet its everyday, lived texture is not fully captured by structured psychometric instruments. Orthopedic clinicians frequently observe that patients who have achieved objective surgical and functional recovery nonetheless remain reluctant to resume movement. This study aimed to explore this phenomenon in patients' own words. We conducted a qualitative netnographic study of 50 first-person Reddit narratives shared by individuals with ACL injury, spanning the rehabilitation trajectory from preoperative anxiety to chronic post-return instability. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis by an interdisciplinary team of orthopedic surgeons and psychiatrists. Three interconnected themes emerged. First, a progressive loss of trust in the injured body, in which normal postoperative sensations were hypervigilantly monitored and catastrophically reinterpreted as signs of graft failure, persisting even after objective strength testing and medical clearance. Second, fear-driven disruption of functional identity and future planning, in which reinjury fear extended beyond the knee to threaten occupational continuity, financial security, and physical self-concept. Third, persistent uncertainty and compulsive reassurance-seeking, fueled by inconsistent rehabilitation guidance and unfavorable social comparison with peers' recovery timelines on social media. Psychological readiness for return to activity appears to be shaped by an interacting network of bodily, identity-related, and informational factors that extend beyond fear of reinjury as traditionally measured. Incorporating expectation management, structured reassurance, and psychologically informed communication into postoperative care protocols may benefit orthopedic and rehabilitation teams. Naturally occurring online narratives may serve as an ecologically valid source of insight into the psychological dimensions of ACL recovery, complementing structured psychometric assessment.
